steps: Calls grant the right to buy and Puts grant the right to sell (100 shares per US contract), with American options exercisable anytime and European only at maturity
Google $550 Long Call ($2,900 cost) earns $7,100 net at $650 with loss capped at $2,900, while a $525 Short Put ($2,240 inflow) loses $2,260 net at $480
Forward hedgers lock fixed prices (ImportCo £10M at $15.742M; ExportCo £30M at $47.208M), eliminating both downside risk and favorable currency upside
Option hedgers buy insurance: 10 July $27.50 Puts for $1,000 protect 1,000 shares at $28 with a $26,500 net floor while keeping full upside
Futures margin ($20,000 controlling £250,000) magnifies gains and losses symmetrically, while options ($2,000 in $22.50 Calls) yield 10x profit ($7,000 at $27) with capped dollar loss
Arbitrageurs buy low in NY ($152) and sell high in London (£100 at $1.55 = $155) to lock in $300 riskless profit per 100 shares until prices converge
Hedge funds (> $2T AUM) charge 2% management and 20% performance fees across Long/Short, Convertible Arb, Merger Arb, Distressed, and Global Macro strategies
Jerome Kerviel's €4.9B SocGen loss (and Leeson's $1B Barings collapse) proves why trading desks require non-negotiable risk limits and independent compliance monitoring
ui_state.bottomTakeaway: Forwards fix prices, options insure floors with asymmetric leverage, arbitrage enforces equilibrium, and strict risk controls prevent rogue wipeouts.
